questions.concept: Agent as a model using tools in a loop
questions.stem: According to the quote 'An agent is a model using tools in a loop,' which statement best describes what an agent is?
options: An agent is a model that uses tools repeatedly in a cycle.
An agent is a person who acts on behalf of another.
An agent is a system that only uses one tool at a time.
An agent is a tool that is used by a model.
questions.source_quote: An agent is a model using tools in a loop.

questions.concept: A feedback loop checks the agent's work
questions.stem: According to the quote, what is the role of the feedback loop?
options: It provides the tools needed for the task.
It controls the entire process.
It checks the work done by the tool loop.
It performs the main task.
questions.source_quote: The tool loop does the work. The feedback loop checks it.

questions.concept: The model decides the next step in the loop
questions.stem: According to the quote, what does the model do in the loop?
options: It decides the next step in the loop by asking for an action.
It executes all steps in the loop by itself.
It runs the action directly without needing any code.
It runs actions on its own without any assistance.
questions.source_quote: The model never runs anything itself. It asks for an action, and ordinary code around it, the harness, runs the action.

questions.concept: The harness is where engineering happens
questions.stem: According to the quote, where does engineering happen?
options: In the model
In the harness
In the code
In the design
questions.source_quote: The harness is everything that is not the model. It is deterministic code, and it is where engineering happens.

questions.stem: According to the quote '95% right per step is 36% right after 20 steps,' which of the following best illustrates the concept that 'errors can compound over time'?
options: After 10 steps, the accuracy drops to 50%.
The accuracy after 20 steps is always higher than the accuracy after 10 steps.
A 1% error per step leads to a 99% error after 20 steps.
If each step has a 5% error rate, the overall accuracy after 20 steps is 36%.
questions.source_quote: 95% right per step is 36% right after 20 steps.
